subject: Clarify: archival/debug snapshots and guarantee we do not train on customer content
messages:

Subject: Clarify: archival/debug snapshots and guarantee we do not train on customer content

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Finli's security team had a few follow-ups about the language around 'we do not train on customer data' in the contract and how that maps to your operational artifacts. Two specific items:

1) Debug snapshots / ephemeral traces: when a customer escalates, do you ever store full request/response snapshots (including customer text) beyond the live incident window for troubleshooting or RCA? If so, how long and are those snapshots used in any internal model development or tuning?

2) Backups / cold archives: what is your retention policy for backups that may contain customer content? Can you confirm backups are excluded from any dataset that might be processed for model training?

We pulled a small export (attached) of the log bundle from a test tenant for context — please flag anything sensitive we should redact. Also, if you have a short written assurance or attestation we can attach to our vendor review, that would help expedite procurement.

Appreciate a short answer and any references to your policy docs or attestation artifacts.

Best,
Emma

Subject: Re: Clarify: archival/debug snapshots and guarantee we do not train on customer content

Hi Emma — thanks for sending this and for the export; helpful example. Short answers up front:

1) Debug snapshots / traces: We retain ephemeral debug snapshots and request/response traces for a limited troubleshooting window (default 30 days). These artifacts are accessible only to on-call and SRE engineers for debugging and RCA. We do NOT use customer request/response snapshots or identifiable logs for model training or fine-tuning.

2) Backups / cold archives: Backups (for disaster recovery) are retained according to the backup TTL configured per account, typically 90 days for hosted customers unless a longer retention is contractually agreed. Backups are treated as an operational artifact and are excluded from any model training pipelines.

A couple of nuance bullets so your reviewers have context:
- Operational telemetry (e.g., aggregated latency histograms, error rates, anonymized token counts) may be used to tune the serving platform; this telemetry does not contain customer text or identifiers.
- Redaction and access controls: snapshots that include customer text are logged to an encrypted, access-controlled bucket; access is audited and requires a documented justification.
- Snapshots used for internal debugging are automatically TTL'd and subject to an internal deletion job that permanently deletes object blobs after the retention window.

We have an attestation template and SOC 2 artifacts I can share; Karthik, can you attach the latest attestation PDF? Marissa, can you confirm the default backup retention and whether we offer a shorter TTL option for customers who require it?

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Security & Trust, Redwood Inference

Emma — adding a couple implementation details to Soojin's note so you can pass along to procurement/security: 

- "Do not train" scope: For hosted and dedicated customers who sign the non-training addendum, we have a contractual commitment that customer-submitted text and request payloads will not be used to train or improve any model weights. This is enforced by pipeline gating: any offline dataset used for modeling is built from curated open-source corpora, synthetic datasets, or opt-in annotated feedback from customers where we have explicit written consent.
- Backup exclusion: Backup jobs write to a separate archival cluster that is logically and operationally treated as never ingested into modeling pipelines; there are policy checks in our data platform that block reads from archival clusters into training buckets without a documented executive approval.
- Long-term retention & forensics exception: In rare incident response cases we may retain a locked snapshot beyond the standard TTL (for example, a preserved evidence copy for a security investigation). Those locked snapshots are encrypted with a restricted key and require CISO-level approval to access; we also record a chain-of-custody and share hashes with the customer on request.
- Evidence & attestation: I'll attach SOC2 and our non-training attestation PDF to this thread.

Let me know if you want a short one-paragraph attestation we can sign for procurement.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
